title: vector-score-contract-and-graceful-upgrade-path
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: We have observed inconsistent reranking scores across clients and SDK versions due to unclear normalization semantics and subtle numerical differences between cosine and raw dot scoring paths. Root causes include (1) mixed assumptions about whether embeddings are pre-normalized, (2) quantized storage (fp16 / int8) losing scale information, (3) zero or near-zero vectors from some models or tokenizers, and (4) divergent client-side post-processing (some SDKs applied L2-normalization, some did not). This leads to user-facing ranking regressions and noisy A/B metrics when switching models or runtimes. Goal: establish a clear, testable server-side score contract, implement a backward-compatible opt-in migration path, and add runtime checks/telemetry to detect regressions early.
acceptance_criteria: Define and publish canonical scoring contract (cosine vs dot) in docs with exact math and edge-case rules
Server exposes explicit score_mode header and response metadata: X-Embed-Score-Mode / embed_score_mode
Clients can opt into new behavior via header; default remains legacy for 4 weeks while collecting telemetry
End-to-end test suite (unit + integration + property tests) reproduces reference numpy/scipy baselines within 1e-6 for fp32 and documents allowable delta for quantized paths
No customer regressions on NDCG@10 or rerank success rate above defined tolerance during canary rollout
proposal_summary: 1) Formalize contract: two canonical modes 'cosine' and 'dot_product' with explicit L2-normalization rules (float32 intermediate), handling for zero vectors (return score 0 and flag), and deterministic tie-breaker behavior. 2) Implement server-side normalization for 'cosine' mode and an opt-in request header 'X-Embed-Score-Mode' that clients can set. 3) Add a compatibility warning header when legacy mode is used and an auditing tool to show per-client score deltas. 4) Provide a migration path: opt-in -> staged default flip after telemetry window. 5) Add telemetry, alerts, and gating in Console and runtime to catch regressions.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: unit + property tests merged behind feature flag (runtime-1.24)
Stage 1: internal canary (platform team + 2 customers) for 48h with detailed telemetry
Stage 2: 1% hosted traffic for 7 days with continuous NDCG/latency monitoring
Stage 3: 10% traffic if metrics stable, then 50% then full roll
Stage 4: after 4 weeks of stable metrics, change default behavior and send deprecation notices to clients still relying on legacy semantics
migration_steps: Publish SDK update and docs with example header usage and code snippets
Expose per-client 'score-delta' dashboard in Console showing median and P95 deltas vs legacy baseline
Provide one-click toggle in Console for enterprises on Dedicated/Private to pin legacy semantics
Offer a compatibility API parameter 'legacy_embed_semantics=true' for a final 12-week grace period
test_matrix: Unit tests: numerical equivalence to numpy for small batches and quantized representations
Property tests: random vectors, extremes (zero, tiny, huge), deterministic tie-breakers
Integration: end-to-end reranker pipelines (embedding -> store -> rerank) against benchmark queries
Performance: latency p50/p95 impact, CPU/GPU normalization cost, throughput under batching
Compatibility: SDKs (python, js, go) exercising opt-in header and legacy path
perf_estimate: Server-side L2 normalization adds ~1.5-3% CPU / token cost in hot paths for typical batch sizes; memory overhead negligible due to streaming normalization. Quantized dot-product paths are unchanged when mode='dot_product'.
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: embed_score_regression if NDCG drop > 2% at P95 across top 10 customers during rollout
Dashboards: per-model and per-client histograms of pre/post normalization vector norms
Log flags: emit embed_score_note for any zero-vector encounter with model_id and request_id
open_risks_and_tradeoffs: Performance: normalization increases CPU on runtime nodes — mitigated by optional hardware-accelerated kernels and batching tweaks
Backcompat complexity: maintaining two modes increases surface area; mitigate with clear default window and Console toggles
Quantized storage: some customers rely on stored scales; server normalization may obscure intended dot-scale semantics — we will document and offer toggles
Edge cases: models that intentionally produce sparse/near-zero vectors must be flagged and handled per-customer
qa_notes: Run the full benchmark set (internal 'rerank-blue') at every rollout step. Capture NDCG, MRR, and top-1 stability. Have a rollback playbook ready to pin legacy semantics by customer. Coordinate with Solutions Engineering for any high-risk customers.
notifications: Announcement draft in #embeddings and #platform-release channels; targeted emails to Dedicated/Private customers one week before default change; release notes entry in 1.24
implementation_notes: Implementation will add a lightweight normalization kernel in the runtime hot path and a request header parser. We will reuse existing batching pipeline; normalization will be applied while building the key-value cache to avoid extra memory passes. Add a small 'compat' shim to the embeddings API layer that records deltas but forwards to legacy scoring when requested.
post_deploy_checks: Verify sample of 10k requests show expected embed_score_mode header in responses
Compare stored embedding norms distribution vs pre-change baseline
Check no regression in throughput greater than 5% on dedicated pools
follow_up_tasks: Create migration playbook for account managers
Add sample notebooks showing how to reproduce score-mode locally
Schedule customer office hours during migration window
notes: Feedback from Design review: call out UX for toggles in Console; make the score mode prominent in API docs
Eng review comment: prefer float32 intermediate for normalization to avoid fp16 drift (accepted)
SRE: ensure metric tag cardinality limited by sampling (will sample 0.5% of requests for delta metric)
